title: us_ai_capex_revenue_scope
text: The five candidate firms disclose large consolidated infrastructure investment, but their audited reports do not provide a harmonized AI-only capex and directly comparable AI revenue series; the user’s $150–200bn capex versus $40bn AI revenue comparison is therefore unverified at issuer-set, period, and accounting-scope level.

title: us_cloud_cash_generates
text: Latest verified reports show substantial consolidated cash generation/liquid resources across the five selected infrastructure operators, while current capex and financing needs differ and some firms are issuing debt or holding restricted escrow; group resources are a buffer, not proof of AI project returns or immunity to a persistent shock.

title: us_ai_willingness_to_pay_unknown
text: Public disclosures now report adoption indicators, including Microsoft more than 30 million M365 Copilot paid seats at FY2026 year-end, but do not identify paid-seat retention/churn, willingness-to-pay elasticity, net AI revenue or margins; productivity evidence does not identify vendor capture.

title: us_commitments_are_heterogeneous
text: Disclosed capital and lease commitments can make infrastructure adjustment costly and delayed, but reported obligations differ in legal firmness, cancellation rights, commencement timing, and whether they are cash or noncash lease commitments; treating all as fixed cash outflows would overstate rigidity.

title: us_quality_adjusted_price_competition
text: Posted API prices, open-weight releases and vendor serving-cost guidance establish credible competitive channels, but quality-, latency-, context-, modality-, batch-, concurrency- and support-adjusted cost per completed workload remains heterogeneous; no matched realized customer switching/price series was found.

title: us_refinancing_transmission_is_lagged
text: Monetary tightening transmits to corporate investment heterogeneously through debt maturity, rollover needs, floating-rate exposure, and distress; a policy-rate increase does not immediately reset every firm’s effective coupon or imply a 10–12% refinancing rate for these hyperscalers.

title: us_rd_displacement_not_yet_observed
text: The inspected 2025 issuer filings disclose substantial R&D spending and, for Meta and Alphabet, increases rather than cuts; they do not establish that a future AI correction or refinancing shock will displace R&D at these firms.

title: us_distressed_sales_not_established
text: The inspected evidence finds no realized distressed hyperscaler datacenter/GPU sale price or recovery sample. Third-party IREN reports FY2026 impairment of USD 638.8m, mainly mining hardware and facility equipment amid conversion to AI cloud; Hyperscale Data disclosed a small mining-equipment impairment during power reallocation to AI compute. These are accounting impairments/strategic conversions, not fire-sale prices or recovery discounts.

title: telecom_analogue_limited
text: WorldCom is a cautionary comparator for network investment, debt service, governance, and restructuring, but its Chapter 11 outcome cannot be attributed to fiber overbuild alone and does not establish that cash-generative hyperscalers face equivalent failure risk.

title: us_utilization_not_comparable_publicly
text: Issuer documents searched through the latest available cutoff filings disclose capacity, capex, revenue, and selected efficiency/throughput indicators but no common named-firm accelerator-hour or server utilization ratio; absence of a comparable public disclosure is a disclosure gap, not evidence of idle capacity.

title: us_apple_exclusion_scope
text: Apple is excluded from the five-firm infrastructure-operator cohort under an explicit scope rule: it is a major device, software, and services platform with cloud services, but its FY2025 filing does not present an external public-cloud infrastructure segment comparable to AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, or Oracle Cloud, nor a comparable AI infrastructure cash-flow bridge.

title: us_paid_seats_are_adoption_not_elasticity
text: Microsoft reports more than 30 million paid M365 Copilot seats at FY2026 year end and reported rapid net adds, enterprise wins and engagement growth; these are dated adoption indicators, not independent estimates of retention, net price, customer ROI, paid-seat churn, or stand-alone AI revenue.

title: us_current_five_company_liquidity_not_uniform
text: The five firms have materially different cash, debt, maturity, financing and contractual exposure; consolidated cash and OCF must be paired with ongoing PPE outlays, scheduled debt, finance lease principal, not-yet-commenced leases, purchase obligations and restricted cash rather than summarized as one sector buffer.

title: us_distressed_asset_evidence_is_impairment_not_sale
text: The current non-hyperscaler evidence found impairment and infrastructure conversion events in adjacent GPU/data-center operators, but not a matched distressed sale with observable transaction price, liens, utilization, or recovery timing; no hyperscaler fire-sale observation is established.

title: us_contractual_cashflow_bridge_reconciled
text: Issuer filings publish meaningful but non-comparable company debt and contractual obligation schedules. Published face principal, balance-sheet carrying debt, lease liabilities, interest-inclusive obligations, and annual purchase commitments have been kept as distinct measures and dated to the source reporting period.

title: us_meta_note8_effective_rate_full_range
text: Meta Note 8 at June 30, 2026 reports a full debt effective interest range of 3.63%–6.48% per year; the 4.27% lower bound applies only to the November 2025 issuance subset.

title: us_oracle_observation_vintages_separate
text: Oracle’s latest interim cash/debt/lease balances are dated August 31, 2026, whereas the published detailed principal maturity ladder is dated May 31, 2026; the bridge retains those vintages separately and does not imply a same-date reconciliation.

title: CN-FLOW-01
text: Revised SAFE 2025 BOP records a USD 735.0bn current-account surplus and USD 773.5bn capital-and-financial-account deficit; the H1 2026 vintage likewise records a USD 378.0bn current-account surplus and USD 345.2bn capital-and-financial-account deficit. Instrument-specific flows, reserves, errors/omissions and valuation must be separated before interpreting private outflows or risk aversion. The 2025 sector/maturity workbook further shows both resident foreign-debt-asset acquisitions and net decreases in bank/general-government portfolio-debt liabilities, so the aggregate deficit masks distinct simultaneous channels.

title: CN-STOCK-01
text: At end-2025 China reported USD 11.786tn external financial assets, USD 7.715tn external liabilities, and USD 4.071tn net external assets; gross position mix and valuation must be kept distinct from liquid private funding capacity.

title: CN-ONSHORE-01
text: Domestic RMB financing is large and distinct from cross-border funding: PBOC/SCIO reports end-June 2026 social financing of RMB 462.06tn, with RMB 279.16tn loans to the real economy and RMB 101.36tn government bonds. Weighted-average rates on newly issued corporate and personal housing loans were about 3.0% and 3.1% respectively in June; none is a borrower-specific LGFV/developer rate.

title: CN-LGFV-01
text: China completed issuance of RMB 2.0tn in 2025 debt-swap bonds; the IMF 2026 Article IV estimates 2025 augmented debt at 126.6% of GDP and its estimated LGFV debt component at 50.9% of GDP. The swap changes maturity, cost and creditor/perimeter classification; it does not by itself extinguish consolidated public-sector liabilities.

title: CN-PROPERTY-01
text: NBS Jan-August 2026 reports real-estate investment down 19.9% y/y, new commercial sales area down 12.1%, developer domestic-loan funding down 33.3% and deposits/advance receipts down 14.8% on comparable/cumulative bases, evidence of weak activity and funding flows but not a measurement of losses, household wealth or completion liabilities.

title: CN-DEMO-01
text: NBS's year-end 2025 annual communiqué reports 851.36m people aged 16–59 (60.6% of population), while the later 1% sample estimates 869.87m aged 15–59 (61.89%); the age bins and survey vintages differ and are not a directly comparable revision.

title: CN-DEMAND-01
text: Evidence supports China domestic-demand weakness and deflationary pressure in the IMF 2026 diagnosis, but does not establish generalized household and healthy-firm balance-sheet deleveraging. September 2026 CPI was positive and latest September PPI was +5.0% y/y, while the living-materials PPI subcomponent remained -0.1% y/y.

title: CN-JAPAN-01
text: Japan's post-bubble balance-sheet repair literature supports analyzing collateral losses, borrower demand and impaired bank transmission as possible channels, but does not identify a Japan-like Chinese trajectory or the probability of prolonged stagnation.

title: CN-EXTDEBT-01
text: At end-June 2026 SAFE measured USD 2.498tn gross external debt, of which USD 1.469tn (59%) was short-term on contractual original maturity; SAFE states 41% of that short-term amount is trade-related credit. Banks held USD 997.4bn and other sectors USD 1,012.7bn, the latter including intercompany lending.

title: CN-LGFV-PERIMETER-01
text: The IMF 2026 Article IV estimate of augmented debt at 126.6% of GDP in 2025 embeds an expanded public perimeter including government-guided funds and LGFV activity; it is not directly comparable to official budgetary debt or an observed stand-alone LGFV balance-sheet total.

title: CN-HOUSEHOLD-BS-01
text: The latest populated PBOC national credit balance sheet located in this closure (November 2025) reports household loans of RMB 83.363tn and household deposits of RMB 163.308tn; these aggregate stocks do not identify mortgage-only exposure or liquidity held by distressed borrower cohorts. PBOC separately reports household loan flows down RMB 0.3668tn in H1 2026, but this is not a June-end stock.

title: CN-DEVELOPER-BS-01
text: China Vanke’s reviewed, unaudited 2026 interim group report text mirror shows 30 June 2026 cash RMB 53.083bn, current borrowings RMB 167.249bn, current bonds RMB 14.461bn, inventory/contract costs RMB 347.967bn, and contract liabilities RMB 77.553bn. The independent review flags RMB 178.86bn principal due within one year and material going-concern uncertainty. These scoped issuer observations demonstrate refinancing/liquidity mismatch for this group, not sector-wide losses or foreign-funding exposure.

title: eu_fiscal_positions_diverge
text: EU sovereign recession vulnerability is heterogeneous: 2026-Q1 gross debt ratios ranged from 25.2% of GDP in Estonia to 143.5% in Greece, while several large economies including France, Italy and Belgium exceeded 100%.

title: ea_foreign_holdings_are_not_safe_haven_flows
text: Foreign ownership of euro-area government bonds is material, but the stock of nonresident holdings does not establish a general safe-haven flow or prove that the euro area will anchor capital during a future shock.

title: crma_benchmarks_are_not_realized_output
text: The CRMA's 2030 extraction, processing and recycling benchmarks express EU capacity ambitions and do not demonstrate that usable annual output, qualified supply or utilization is already available.

title: kiruna_resource_not_current_mine_output
text: LKAB's Per Geijer rare-earth estimate is a mineral resource and a prospective source, not a reserve or current mine production; conversion to market supply requires permitting, feasibility, construction, recovery and downstream separation.

title: europe_rare_earth_refining_pipeline_is_conditional
text: European rare-earth processing and magnet projects have moved beyond announcement at some stages—Narva began limited commercial magnet production in 2026—but evidence does not establish audited annual output or utilization. Caremag is financed and planned for late-2026 commissioning, not evidenced as operating by the 2026-10-14 cutoff. Narva is magnet manufacturing; Caremag is a planned recycling/separation/refining facility, and project designation is not throughput.

title: recycling_30pct_sufficiency_unsubstantiated
text: The alleged roughly 30% EU permanent-magnet recycling sufficiency is not established. A primary source does report Solvay’s corporate objective to satisfy 30% of European rare-earth demand by 2030, but that is a forward-looking company objective for rare-earth production, not an observed EU-wide recycled-magnet input share; the source does not provide a matched denominator or audited throughput.

title: automotive_hybrid_deal_misstates_status
text: No verified March 2026 EU-wide hybrid agreement was found in the primary legal record as of 2026-10-14. Regulation (EU) 2023/851 remains the enacted baseline; COM(2025) 995 proposes a 90% rather than 100% 2035 fleet reduction, but the ordinary legislative procedure 2025/0420/COD remained ongoing at retrieval. March and June 2026 Council records describe debate/progress, not adoption; the distinct 2025–27 compliance averaging measure is enacted.

title: ea_growth_not_broad_demand_proof
text: Euro-area Q2 2026 GDP increased 0.6% quarter on quarter, but the expenditure composition included a negative inventory contribution and a positive net-export contribution, so headline growth alone is not evidence of broad domestic-demand resilience.

title: solvay_30pct_is_a_company_goal_not_recycling_observation
text: Solvay’s April 2025 statement that its La Rochelle expansion is a first step toward satisfying 30% of European rare-earth demand by 2030 is a company objective; the release does not report an achieved 30% share, disclose a tonnes-per-year plant output, or identify the objective as recycled permanent-magnet feed alone.

title: eu_private_debt_latest_q2_2026
text: ECB Q2 2026 euro-area sector accounts report non-financial corporation debt at 66.0% of GDP on a consolidated basis and 135.6% on a wider non-consolidated basis, while household debt was 80.3% of disposable income; these are euro-area aggregates, not EU27 totals.

title: eu_bank_resilience_perimeter_2026q2
text: Q2 2026 bank capital evidence is strong in both the ECB Significant Institution subset and the EBA EU/EEA dashboard, but the measures have different supervisory and geographic perimeters and do not identify country-level US/China credit exposure.

title: eu_crossborder_bank_claims_us_china_partial
text: BIS Q1 2026 consolidated banking data identify material EU-reporter bank claims on US and China counterparties, but published coverage differs by country and risk basis and cannot be interpreted as complete EU totals.

title: eu_recycling_not_exact_30pct
text: A source-linked cohort and mass-balance review does not establish that EU magnet recycling can supply exactly 30% of demand in the 2030s; a 2022 selected-application model estimates 8–19% secondary supply/demand during 2025–2030, 16–34% in 2040 and 24–48% in 2050, subject to modeled assumptions and incomplete market coverage.

title: eu_magnet_stock_flow_known_unknowns
text: Available lifetime and cohort evidence implies substantial lag between magnet deployment and end-of-life feed: modeled EV retirements become material around 2035, while 2020s feed is dominated by earlier product cohorts; manufacturing scrap and complete Nd/Pr/Dy/Tb composition remain unquantified in the located EU evidence.

title: CHF_SAFE_HAVEN_BILATERAL
text: CHF appreciation during global risk episodes is bilateral and time-varying, rather than a universal rise against every currency.

title: CHF_IMPORT_DISINFLATION
text: A CHF appreciation can lower Swiss import prices and consumer inflation, but pass-through depends on invoice currency and is attenuated at aggregate CPI level.

title: SWISS_INFLATION_FORECAST_06
text: SECO's September 2026 forecast supports 0.6% average inflation in both 2026 and 2027, while the SNB's later September policy assessment projects 0.7% and 0.8% conditional averages.

title: PHARMA_EXPORTS_ANCHOR
text: Chemicals and pharmaceuticals materially support Swiss merchandise exports and drove an unusually large portion of Q2 2026 GDP growth, making aggregate resilience sensitive to volatile sector output.

title: MERCHANTING_CA_NOT_GDP
text: Swiss commodity merchanting can materially move measured goods and current-account balances without an equivalent change in domestic production or GDP.

title: EU_PACKAGE_SIGNED_NOT_IN_FORCE
text: The Switzerland–EU package agreements were signed in March 2026 and sent to Parliament, but signature and dispatch do not establish general ratification or entry into force.

title: ELECTRICITY_MARKET_ACCESS_STATUS_QUO
text: Switzerland's physical integration with the EU electricity system without legal guarantees creates a plausible security-of-supply and trading friction channel; a signed electricity agreement is a prospective pathway pending process.

title: FRIENDSHORING_RESILIENCE
text: Swiss openness, specialized exports and EU market access create both supply-chain resilience options and exposure to external demand, regulatory and concentration shocks; a net friendshoring gain is not established by available aggregate evidence.

title: HORIZON_PROGRAMME_ACCESS_DISTINCT_FROM_PACKAGE
text: Swiss participation in Horizon Europe, Euratom and Digital Europe from programme year 2025 follows the separately signed EU Programmes Agreement, provisionally applied retroactively from 1 January 2025; this does not put the full March 2026 Bilaterals III package into force, and programme-call exceptions remain.

title: SWISS_2015_EXPORT_QUANTITY_RESILIENCE
text: The 2015 CHF appreciation did not produce a statistically significant decline in aggregate real Swiss goods export quantities in a synthetic-control study, while nominal CHF exports fell about 7% in the short run and sector responses differed sharply.

title: SWISS_MERCHANTING_GROSS_TURNOVER
text: SNB balance-of-payments data record large gross merchanting sales flows, but those gross flows are not equivalent to Swiss domestic value added, GDP or local financing exposure.

title: SWISS_INPUT_DIVERSIFICATION
text: Pre-2022 evidence indicates Swiss import dependencies were generally diversified and average product-level import concentration fell, although some critical country-product dependencies persisted and external-input reliance remained concentrated in EU-sourced inputs.

title: FOCBS_Q1_2026_CHEM_PHARMA_QQ
text: FOCBS Annex Ia reports seasonally adjusted nominal Swiss chemical and pharmaceutical exports of CHF 33,652 million in 2026-Q1, down 8.1% quarter on quarter from 2025-Q4.

title: MERCHANTING_NET_Q2_2026_QUANTIFICATION
text: The SNB reports that the merchanting balance rose significantly year on year in 2026-Q2, but the located current-account cube gives only the aggregate net current-account balance and the located merchanting cube gives gross sales.

title: global-bank-credit-not-contracting-q1-2026
text: At end-Q1 2026, the measured BIS cross-border bank-credit aggregate was expanding, so this specific available aggregate contradicts the proposition that the measured global bank-credit stock was already contracting.

title: global-amplification-through-balance-sheets
text: A common rate, risk or currency shock can amplify real activity losses when repricing, maturity rollover, collateral valuation, leverage and intermediary liquidity constraints jointly weaken financing and cash flow.

title: usd-funding-mismatch-transmits-across-borders
text: Pre-crisis foreign-currency asset growth funded through short-term wholesale and FX-swap markets created dollar rollover needs for non-US banks, and market impairment transmitted dollar funding stress internationally in 2007–09.

title: risk-sensitive-portfolio-flows-can-amplify-stress
text: Cross-border portfolio funding intermediated by some risk-sensitive nonbank investors can transmit global risk repricing into tighter financing conditions for recipient economies, especially where prior vulnerabilities are high.

title: cross-region-network-co-movement-not-causal-multiplier
text: Selected 2024 official merchandise-trade flows and Q1 2026 BIS bank-nationality claims demonstrate cross-region links, but the partial links do not identify a complete bilateral exposure matrix, net positions, or a causal spillover coefficient for US, China, EU and Switzerland.

title: positions-transactions-and-valuation-must-be-separated
text: External positions are stocks that change through transactions, exchange-rate and price valuation, and other volume/reclassification changes; gross claims and liabilities cannot be interpreted as net funding flows or losses without reconciliation.

title: historical-credit-booms-inform-stress-not-probability
text: Long-run cross-country evidence finds credit-intensive expansions are followed on average by deeper recessions and slower recoveries, supporting a conditional balance-sheet stress mechanism but not a calibrated probability for this scenario.

title: goods-price-deflation-is-not-automatically-debt-deflation
text: Historical BIS analysis finds a weak unconditional relation between consumer-price deflation and output growth, while asset/property-price deflation has a stronger adverse association and private debt can amplify property-price downturns.

title: telecom-overbuild-analogue-has-limits
text: Telecom overbuild and bankrupt carrier cases can inform tests of synchronized capacity investment, utilization, price competition, debt service and asset recovery, but cannot establish hyperscaler losses or crisis likelihood.

title: ai capex revenue mismatch
text: Cash capex for servers, buildings and power is paid before or during capacity ramp; if incremental AI receipts and margins do not catch up, net capex lowers group free cash flow and eventually constrains investment or requires financing. AI-specific revenue and capex attribution is not comparable across the candidate firms, so the hypothesized mismatch is not established by consolidated statements.

title: willingness to pay
text: Perceived incremental quality and workflow return influence adoption, paid-seat expansion, renewals, usage and realized price; lower value or abundant alternatives can reduce each, while compliance, integration and switching costs can support retention. Revenue converts to cash after billing/collection and may be bundled.

title: fixed commitments
text: Long lead-time power, land, buildings, chips and lease commitments can obligate cash after expected demand weakens; unavoidable fixed costs then worsen operating leverage and defer capacity adjustment. Cancellation, deferral and resale rights determine the actual short-run rigidity.

title: pricing competition
text: New model entrants, open weights, efficiency gains or lower inference costs can drive down quality-adjusted prices; that may expand volume or compress vendor margins depending on demand elasticity, cost decline and differentiated service value.

title: refinancing spreads
text: Higher benchmark yields or issuer spreads raise cost on new borrowing and reset/floating debt; at maturity, rollover turns new rates into debt service, reducing free cash flow and possibly investment, hiring or refinancing capacity. Cash buffers and long fixed coupons delay transmission.

title: rd displacement
text: A shortfall in internal cash or external finance can force management to ration discretionary spending; projects with long payback, weaker expected returns or less strategic priority may be delayed, including R&D. A rate shock can also reduce investment opportunities independently of financing constraints.

title: distressed asset sales
text: If revenues fall while fixed obligations, debt service and financing constraints persist, a distressed owner may restructure, impair, sell, or abandon assets. Specialized assets may clear below replacement cost if site, grid, cooling, hardware generation or buyer access is limiting.

title: telecom 2001 analogue
text: Telecom network construction, expectations about traffic and revenues, debt and fixed network costs, plus governance/accounting quality can interact; lower realized demand or financing access can produce write-downs, restructuring and creditor losses.

title: utilization disclosure
text: Capacity installed ahead of use creates depreciation, power and lease costs before serving revenue; utilization can improve unit economics as demand fills capacity, while idle or mismatched specialized assets reduce realized returns. Provisioned capacity, utilized accelerator time, power draw and revenue are different quantities.

title: foreign capital channels
text: A global risk-off shock can reduce foreign portfolio and debt claims, slow FDI, raise offshore rollover costs and pressure FX expectations; those effects reach domestic activity only through exposed borrowers, asset prices, confidence or reserve/intervention channels. SAFE's 2025 external-flow mix is the starting point, not a causal test of Western risk aversion.

title: onshore funding
text: External funding stress can spill into domestic RMB activity if banks face FX/liquidity pressure, confidence weakens or local borrowers lose refinancing access; PBoC liquidity, deposit funding, state-bank rollover and fiscal transfers can damp that link. Effective loan prices and credit allocation, not LPR alone, govern borrower cash flow.

title: lgfv deleveraging
text: Lower land-sale revenue and weak project cash generation can reduce local fiscal capacity, impair LGFV debt service, induce refinancing or forced asset sales, and crowd out local investment/services; creditor losses or risk transfer may then affect banks and the central/local fiscal balance. Debt swaps can buy time through term and rate relief.

title: property balance sheet
text: Lower property sales and prices reduce developer presale and financing receipts, constrain completion, impair developer asset values and household housing wealth, and weaken land revenue; lower construction and consumption can then feed back to local budgets and bank collateral/asset quality. Completion guarantees, restructuring and price adjustment can interrupt or redistribute the chain.

title: demographics
text: Aging and changing cohort sizes gradually affect labor-force entry/exit, household formation, housing demand, savings composition, pension and health spending, and the tax base; hours, participation, migration, retirement policy and productivity mediate the impact on output and per-capita welfare.

title: consumption deflation
text: Property losses, uncertain income and weak confidence can raise precautionary saving or debt repair and lower consumption; weak demand may lower goods prices and nominal income, raising real debt burdens where nominal debts are sticky and feeding back into spending. Fiscal transfers, real wage gains, cheaper imports and exports can offset the loop.

title: japan balance sheet analogue
text: After a collateral boom, firms may prioritize debt repayment over investment, households reduce borrowing, and banks delay loss recognition; impaired credit allocation and weak nominal demand can prolong repair. Policy recapitalization, write-downs, income support and asset-price stabilization can shorten it. Japan history makes these channels plausible, not inevitable for China.

title: debt exposures
text: A regional recession reduces tax bases and nominal GDP while automatic stabilizers, transfers and support raise borrowing; debt/GDP and issuance rise. Higher sovereign yields feed bank, firm and household benchmark costs, with country-specific pass-through shaped by duration, fixed coupons, refinancing needs, fiscal institutions and ECB transmission. Interactions among sovereign risk, bank holdings, credit supply and private demand can reinforce or dampen the initial shock.

title: safe haven flows
text: A global or regional shock changes relative expected safety, liquidity, currency and return across assets; foreign investors rebalance euro-area sovereign securities, altering bond demand, yields and spreads. Flow direction differs across countries, maturities, investor types and currencies; ECB purchases/redemptions, hedging costs and domestic institutions can offset or amplify it. Lower sovereign yields may ease bank and corporate funding, while withdrawals can tighten conditions and interact with sovereign-bank holdings.

title: critical minerals production
text: Import concentration or trade disruption constrains rare-earth feedstock and magnet availability; extraction projects can diversify ore supply only after resource conversion, permitting, financing, construction, recovery and transport. Extraction alone is insufficient without separation/refining, qualified alloy/magnet production and downstream customers. Supply shortfalls can delay EV, wind and electronics production or raise input prices; substitution and inventory drawdowns are partial buffers.

title: refining capacity
text: Even if mined or recycled material exists, separation and refining bottlenecks can constrain usable rare-earth oxides; alloy and magnet manufacturing then require process qualification, scale, energy, chemicals, technical labor and customer certification. A plant's commissioning/ramp and utilization determine the flow that can substitute for imports. Capacity shortfalls can create input scarcity, higher costs, delayed production and weak returns that in turn threaten project financing.

title: magnet recycling stock flow
text: Permanent magnets embedded in vehicles, turbines, appliances and equipment enter the in-use stock for years; product lifetime, collection, disassembly and sorting determine when and how much magnet scrap becomes feed. Recovery and separation yields determine secondary rare-earth output; demand can grow faster than this lagged waste flow, so new recycling plants may initially compete for limited feedstock. Recycling can reduce virgin imports over time but cannot be inferred from generic waste recycling rates or nameplate capacity.

title: automotive hybrid agreement status
text: Automotive CO2 rules and fleet compliance periods alter manufacturers' product mix, investment timing, emissions-credit needs and demand for battery, hybrid and combustion technologies. An enacted target or amendment changes binding constraints; Commission proposals and Council working documents do not. Misstating a proposal as an adopted hybrid exception would distort transition-path assumptions for auto demand, investment, critical-material requirements and supply-chain cash flows.

title: chf appreciation
text: A global risk shock or relative-yield change alters bilateral CHF demand; the exchange rate then changes foreign-currency revenue and input costs, importer prices, exporter markups and volumes, and monetary conditions. SNB FX intervention and policy rates can alter or lean against the move. The direction depends on the countercurrency and shock, not a single global CHF index.

title: import inflation snb
text: CHF appreciation reduces the CHF price of foreign goods according to invoice currency and price-setting behavior; retailers and importers pass some change into consumer goods with lags. Energy, domestic services, rents, margins and the SNB policy response jointly determine CPI. CHF weakness or global commodity inflation can reverse the import disinflation contribution.

title: pharma chemical exports
text: Foreign demand, regulatory access, product mix and CHF valuation affect high-value chemical/pharmaceutical export receipts; imported inputs, global pricing, local production, hedges and intellectual-property rents affect domestic value added. A temporary output or inventory shift can swing quarterly GDP and customs totals without indicating durable economy-wide demand.

title: commodity trading
text: Global commodity prices, trade finance, sanctions and counterparty risk affect Swiss merchanting turnover and margins; transactions can alter gross cross-border goods flows and the current account although goods are bought and resold abroad. Margins, services, employment and local taxes are the domestic transmission; financing and collateral links can amplify global liquidity stress.

title: eu market access
text: Regulatory divergence, mutual-recognition coverage and institutional uncertainty affect fixed costs, certification, supply chains and investment for Swiss firms selling into the EU; a negotiated package may reduce some frictions after ratification, implementation and entry into force. Existing sector-specific discontinuities make the channel credible but do not quantify whole-economy costs.

title: electricity research pathways
text: Physical electricity interconnection and research networks connect Switzerland to EU markets. Without legal guarantees and full institutional participation, cross-border scheduling/trading, system balancing and research collaboration face uncertainty; an electricity agreement can improve security, trading and grid stability, while programme-specific research association restores eligibility subject to call rules and financing.

title: friendshoring
text: Geopolitical fragmentation or supply restrictions can lead Swiss firms to diversify suppliers, inventories, production locations and customer markets toward trusted partners. Diversification can improve resilience but may increase costs, reduce scale economies or simply relocate concentration; openness and EU market access shape feasible options.

title: global liquidity feedbacks
text: A policy/inflation/supply shock raises risk-free rates, term premia, FX basis or borrower-specific spreads; asset repricing and margin/collateral calls may constrain intermediaries; maturing liabilities then refinance at higher costs or fail to roll; weaker cash flow and investment can lower collateral and repayment capacity, creating lender losses and tighter credit. Central-bank facilities can bridge solvent institutions facing liquidity pressure, while fiscal restructuring, recapitalization or loss allocation is needed for insolvency.

title: cross border capital feedbacks
text: A source-country rate/risk repricing can lead foreign investors or lenders to rebalance; portfolio, bank, FDI and trade-credit exposures can transmit through prices, rollover needs, FX demand and affiliate earnings. Currency depreciation can raise local-currency debt burdens for unhedged borrowers, while weaker collateral and cash flow can tighten credit. Local-currency funding, capital controls, reserves, hedges, domestic investors, trade substitution and policy support alter each regional link. The refreshed BIS CBS panel contains seven numeric 2026-Q1 gross international-claim observations reported by FR- and GB-nationality banking groups on DE, CH, US and FR residents; it returned no numeric rows for the selected US, CN or CH reporter series, or for selected CN counterpart-residence combinations. GB is not an EU reporter, and bank nationality is not country residence. The bounded 2024 UN Comtrade comparison provides four observed reporter-export flows (US↔China and EU27→US/China); Swiss-pair and US→EU requests returned no rows. A separate 2018 OECD input-output proxy records EU suppliers at 54% of Swiss imported intermediate inputs. These measures bound links only; none is a causal output multiplier.

title: historical analogue limits
text: Historical episodes supply conditional sequences: credit-intensive investment and collateral expansion can precede deeper recessions; after losses, leverage, fixed obligations and limited refinancing can propagate the shock. A telecom infrastructure analogue can motivate testing oversupply, utilization, pricing, debt and salvage; the 2008–09 dollar funding crisis illustrates currency/maturity mismatch; property-price deflation episodes show collateral and private debt can interact. Whether mechanisms transfer depends on balance sheets, institutions, product demand, technology reuse, policy response and timing.
